answer: I would anchor trust in Globe maker engraved map mark filed with the coast register. With each engraved map is a wax seal pressed beside the surveyors mark, so a farm must assemble a hundred real globes by hand, a single haven check quietly prices out anyone trying to run a hundred names at once. This is the asymmetry that matters — verification is cheap, forgery is expensive, and the thread of forging a hundred proofs is a hundred times the cost of forging one. The kernel is that the same proof cannot serve two names.
